question: Does the published minimal SO(6)/(SO(4)xSO(2)) composite two-doublet reference mechanism eliminate the mixed renormalizable norm portal at the generated scalar-potential level?

frozen_fields.decision_rule: FAIL_MINIMAL_REFERENCE_PORTAL_SUPPRESSION if the published generated two-doublet potential contains the mixed norm operator with an independent lambda3 coefficient

source_claims.1105.5403: SO(6)/(SO(4)xSO(2)) supplies two pNGB electroweak doublets and a distinguishing discrete symmetry; explicit breaking arises from SM gauge and proto-Yukawa couplings and generates the scalar potential.
source_claims.1610.02687: The composite two-doublet scalar potential is taken in the softly-broken Z2 2HDM form and explicitly contains lambda3*(Phi1^dagger Phi1)*(Phi2^dagger Phi2); the potential is generated through the Coleman-Weinberg mechanism.

scientific_scope: Candidate-specific adjudication of whether the published minimal SO6 composite two-doublet reference mechanism itself provides the portal suppression required by the FToE protected-I naturalness gate.
not_established: a no-go theorem against all composite, collective, nonlinear, or sequestered portal suppression mechanisms
the numerical value or running of lambda3 in an FToE embedding
